sources.title: C11 intptr_t and uintptr_t
sources.sections_read: Cover date; 6.3.2.3 pointer/integer conversions; 7.20.1.4 intptr_t and uintptr_t (find read 2026-11-20 11:02:06 UTC).
sources.confirmed: N1570 dated April 12, 2011 specifies optional signed and unsigned integer types that preserve valid void-pointer values through a round trip. General integer-to-pointer conversion is implementation-defined and can yield misalignment or an invalid representation.
sources.limits: These types are optional; general pointer/integer mappings are implementation-defined, and modified integer values need not form valid pointers. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C23.json.

sources.sections_read: Versioned manual; ptrtoint and inttoptr instruction semantics (find read 2026-11-20 11:02:06 UTC).
sources.confirmed: The 3.7.0 manual specifies pointer-to-integer and integer-to-pointer conversion, with truncation or zero extension when widths differ and no bit change when widths match.
sources.limits: Width mismatches truncate or zero-extend; a frontend still needs an API and rules for valid reconstructed pointers. sources.title: Rust raw-pointer and usize casts
sources.sections_read: Pointer-to-address casts; address-to-pointer casts; pointer arithmetic example (find read 2026-11-20 11:02:50 UTC).
sources.confirmed: The live Rust Reference uses raw-pointer casts to usize and back, explains narrower integer truncation, and gives an address-arithmetic example subject to aliasing and memory-model restrictions.
sources.limits: Narrower integers can truncate addresses, and bitwise equality does not establish pointer validity or permission to dereference. sources.title: Go unsafe.Pointer and uintptr conversion patterns
sources.sections_read: unsafe.Pointer conversion patterns 2–4 and uintptr lifetime caveat; targeted finds 2026-11-20 11:03:14 UTC.
sources.confirmed: Go documents arithmetic and alignment masking through uintptr, plus conversion directly in syscall argument lists. Integer address values do not retain or track objects, so round trips are constrained.
sources.limits: Go's garbage-collector rules require constrained conversions and object lifetimes; those rules need deliberate translation to another language. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C23.json.

sources.title: LLVM PointerIntPair
sources.sections_read: PointerIntPair getters/setters, masks, low-bit traits, alignment and tag-width assertions; targeted finds 2026-11-20 11:03:14 UTC.
sources.confirmed: The header packs pointer and integer fields using masks and shifts, validates available low bits and alignment, and extracts an untagged pointer through getPointer.
sources.limits: Only alignment-provided low bits are available; tag width and pointer alignment must satisfy the implementation's checks. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C23.json.

sources.title: C++ explicit reinterpret_cast pointer/integer conversion
sources.sections_read: N3337 section 5.2.10 paragraphs 4–5; targeted finds at 2026-11-20 11:03:14 UTC and 2026-11-20 11:03:37 UTC.
sources.confirmed: N3337 allows pointer conversion to sufficiently wide integers and guarantees restoration on conversion back to the same pointer type; other mappings remain implementation-defined.
sources.limits: The mapping is implementation-defined; the round-trip guarantee does not validate arbitrary arithmetic-modified addresses.
